::: {#exr-radius}
## Radius of convergence

::: {.lm-solution}
With the ratio test, $\sum a_k x^k$ converges for $|x| < R = \lim |a_k / a_{k+1}|$. Here $|a_k / a_{k+1}| = 2^{k+1} / 2^k = 2$, so $R = 2$.

For $x = 1$, inside the radius, the series is the geometric series with $q = 1/2$ and converges to $1 / (1 - 1/2) = 2$. For $x = 3$, outside the radius, the terms $(3/2)^k$ grow, and the series diverges.
:::
:::

::: {#exr-taylor}
## Taylor polynomials of the exponential function

### Implementation

::: {.lm-solution}
```{r}
taylor_exp <- function(x, n) {
  term <- 1
  total <- 1
  for (k in seq_len(n)) {
    term <- term * x / k
    total <- total + term
  }
  total
}
```
:::

### Errors

::: {.lm-solution}
```{r}
ns <- 1:15
errors <- abs(sapply(ns, function(n) taylor_exp(1, n)) - exp(1))
kable(data.frame(n = ns, error = format(errors, digits = 3)))
```

The error is about $1 / (n + 1)!$, the first term left out. It falls faster and faster; after about $17$ terms, it reaches the level of the rounding errors.
:::
:::
